findings.explanation: The docker stats CLI prints a table by default and, with --format json, exposes network traffic only as a human-readable NetIO string such as "1.2kB / 648B"; it has no tx_bytes, rx_bytes, tx_dropped or rx_dropped fields. Those per-interface counters exist only in the Docker Engine API /containers/{id}/stats response under networks.<iface>. A reader building a docker stats poller as described would never get the fields the SPL needs.
findings.quote: per-container cumulative tx_bytes, rx_bytes, tx_dropped, and rx_dropped fields parsed from docker stats --no-trunc --no-stream JSON
findings.suggested_fix: Say the poller must call the Engine API stats endpoint (GET /containers/{id}/stats?stream=false) and flatten networks.<iface>.rx_bytes, tx_bytes, rx_dropped, tx_dropped per interface, or use cAdvisor container_network_* counters. Apply the same correction to detailedImplementation Step 2, which repeats the docker stats JSON Lines claim.

findings.explanation: Splunk_TA_nix ships no linux:proc:net:dev sourcetype, no per-container network-namespace input and no docker stats wrapper; its network inputs are interfaces.sh and bandwidth.sh at host level. The text reads as if the TA provides this collection out of the box.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ([Splunkbase 833](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/833)) for linux:proc:net:dev scripted collection and docker stats wrapper scripts
findings.suggested_fix: State that linux:proc:net:dev and the stats poller are custom scripted inputs the operator writes (optionally packaged in a local app deployed alongside Splunk_TA_nix), and describe the /proc/<pid>/net/dev parsing required since that file is a whitespace table, not key=value fields.

findings.explanation: Network_Traffic models flow/session records with src, dest and ports; cumulative per-container interface byte and drop counters are not flows and carry no destination. The signal fits the Performance data model's Network dataset (thruput) far better, if any CIM model.
findings.suggested_fix: Map to Performance (Network dataset) only, or drop CIM mapping and state that the UC runs on raw sourcetypes; keep Network_Traffic only as an optional corroborating source for flow data that names destinations.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no Windows filter, no host-network-mode filter and no maintenance lookup; the only lookup is container_egress_baseline.csv. The exclusions describe behaviour the search does not implement.
findings.quote: Skips Windows containers where counter semantics differ. Ignores intentionally high-throughput batch jobs that are pre-registered in a maintenance lookup.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe these as scoping decisions the operator must enforce at collection time, or name the concrete lookup and the where clause the operator must add; do not claim the search skips them.

findings.explanation: With latest=@h the window only moves once per hour, so a five-minute schedule re-evaluates identical data twelve times an hour and cannot see the most recent up-to-59 minutes; the search also returns every qualifying 5m bucket in the six-hour window, so each run re-alerts on old buckets.
findings.quote: schedule container_uc_3_1_23_network_io_anomalies every five minutes over earliest=-6h@h
findings.suggested_fix: Explain the latency and duplication trade-off, and recommend either an hourly schedule or a latest=@5m window with alerting restricted to the newest bucket plus throttling on host_id and container_id.

findings.explanation: This is generator/authoring checklist residue (also 'Fenced SPL for runbooks must match the spl JSON field byte-for-byte', 'JSON narratives contain no asterisk emphasis pairs', and 'Case 12 — finance challenges ingest cost'), not implementation guidance. Unsupported specifics like 'topping fifty thousand containers' and 'Mirantis Container Runtime versus Docker CE field naming deltas' are invented context.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: five Step headers with em dashes; multisearch lists docker:stats and linux:proc:net:dev; streamstats differences cumulative counters; eventstats supplies host totals and per-container mu and sigma; join wraps inputlookup container_egress_baseline.csv; severity uses only the mandated tier strings; closing table lists thirteen analyst columns
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the closing checklist, the byte-for-byte note and the finance case; remove the invented fleet size and the unverified Mirantis field-naming claim.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by a generic repo handle with no SME sign-off evidence, while its collection path cannot produce the fields the SPL uses.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until an SME validates the collector output against the SPL.

findings.explanation: This Lantern path may not exist (Lantern data-source pages use different slugs). The cgroup v2 reference is also off-topic: cgroup v2 provides no network byte or drop counters, which live per network namespace.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the Lantern URL resolves or replace it; replace the cgroup v2 reference with the Docker Engine API ContainerStats reference and the Linux /proc/net/dev documentation. Remove the 'Linux cgroup v2 documentation' mention from evidence.

findings.explanation: The SPL triggers at three standard deviations, a 60 percent host-share, or drop rates; 'a hundred times' overstates the threshold, and dropped packets (a major alert tier) are not mentioned.
findings.quote: When one dock suddenly ships a hundred times its usual weight while the others go quiet
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'much more than usual, or more than half of everything leaving the floor', and add a clause about packages getting lost on the way out.

findings.explanation: GitHub is only where cAdvisor source code is hosted; it is not equipment monitored by this UC.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove github from equipment; keep docker and, if cAdvisor is in scope, prometheus/cadvisor.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The 'sustained two consecutive buckets' gate does not work: streamstats window=2 current=t last(host_egress_share_pct) AS prev_share returns the current row's value (the last event in a window that includes the current event), so sustained_share_gt60 is true whenever the current bucket alone exceeds 60. Use current=f window=1 (or window=2 current=t first()) to get the previous bucket.

tx_bytes_per_min is the sum of per-sample per-minute rates inside each 5m bucket, so at a 60s poll it is about five times the real per-minute rate (and doubles again when both lanes report the same container); the >500 drop thresholds and the z-score therefore depend on poll cadence and lane overlap. Also the proc lane leaves image empty, splitting the same container into separate stats groups. Use avg() or recompute rate from bucket deltas, and dedupe lanes.

latest=@h with a five-minute schedule re-scans the same hour, and the search emits every qualifying bucket across six hours, so alerts repeat for old buckets; low_baseline_drift_no_history fires for every bucket of every container lacking a baseline row, flooding output.

nodename=Performance.HostPerformance and the field Performance.cpu_load_percent do not exist in the CIM Performance data model (root dataset All_Performance; CPU is All_Performance.CPU.cpu_load_percent with nodename=All_Performance.CPU). CPU load is also unrelated to network I/O; the Network dataset (thruput) would be the relevant one.

T1048 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol) and T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) assert protocol-level behaviour that byte counters cannot distinguish; volume-based detection aligns more closely with T1030 (Data Transfer Size Limits) or T1041 only with corroborating flow data.

summary: The detection idea (per-container egress share, z-score and drop-rate tiers from cumulative counters) is sound and the implementation narrative is detailed, but the collection path is factually wrong (docker stats CLI does not emit tx_bytes/rx_dropped fields), the CIM mapping and cimSpl do not fit, the SPL's 'sustained' logic does not do what the prose says, and the long implementation text carries authoring residue.
